title: A height-one valuation ring admits a real absolute value
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $V\subset F$ a valuation subring [def-trf-valuation-ring], with $F$ its fraction field. Suppose that $V$ is not a field and its only prime ideals are $(0)$ and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Then there is a function $|\cdot|:F\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ with $|x|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $|1|=1$, $|xy|=|x||y|$ and $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$, such that $V=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ and $\mathfrak m=\{x:|x|<1\}$. This absolute value is nontrivial.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp. 6–7: valuation rings, prime ideals and convex subgroups; the height-one/real-valued bridge used at Theorem 3.5.5 Step 3.
